title: FY2027 Administration R&D Budget Priorities (M-25-34 / NSTM-2) — Phase 65 Quantum review
publisher: Office of Management and Budget and Office of Science and Technology Policy
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Quantum reporting pack. M-25-34 and NSTM-2 direct agencies to align FY2027 R&D with critical and emerging technologies, energy, national security, health and biotechnology, and space. AI, quantum, semiconductors, advanced communications, advanced manufacturing, critical minerals, and the infrastructure beneath them are treated as a connected federal portfolio.
key_findings: AI priorities include new architectures, efficiency, evaluation, security, scientific discovery, autonomy, and structured datasets.
Quantum, semiconductors, communications, manufacturing, energy, minerals, biotechnology, and space are framed as mutually supporting national capabilities.
The memorandum links research choices to economic growth, high-wage employment, and national security.
why_it_matters: Which records separate quantum research and migration policy from standards, procurement, tested interoperability, accepted cutover, and retired cryptography? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. It is the clearest cross-government statement of which technical and physical systems agencies were told to prioritize in the FY2027 budget cycle.
ftfn_relevance: Supports a federal portfolio map across AI, compute, power, materials, manufacturing, and security.
Provides a policy baseline against which agency budgets, solicitations, and awards can be compared.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
Budget guidance shapes agency submissions but does not itself appropriate funds.
The priorities are broad and do not guarantee specific programs, awards, or outcomes.
